title_original: Enrica Perez’s ‘On Top Of The Cliff’ wins top prize at Tallinn Black Nights
excerpt_original: The Peru-set thriller also took home best actress.

blocks.text: Source: POFF
‘On Top Of The Cliff’
Enrica Perez’s On Top Of The Cliff won the Grand Prix for best film at the 30th Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (POFF).

The thriller follows a teenage girl at a Catholic boarding school in 1950s Peru whose status quo is tested by the arrival of a rebellious foreigner. It is a co-production between Mexico, Peru and Switzerland.
Scroll down for full list of winners

The top prize carries a €20,000 grant from the City of Tallinn which Is shared between Perez and producers Enid Campos, Martha Orozco and Joël Jent. The film’s star Bianca Bucelli took home best actress.

On awarding On Top Of The Cliff , the jury was “especially impressed by the high quality of every department of this film – direction, script, acting, cinematography, design and music – combining to create a hermetic universe, intense, powerful and visually eloquent.”

The best director award went to Swiss director Fred Baillif for his social work drama A Job Well Done , while German-Vietnamese filmmaker Alison Kuhn took home best script for her crime drama The Matriarch .
The jury for the official competition comprised Christopher Hampton, David Stump, Julie Billy, Tiina Tauraite, and Myriam Sassine.

In the first feature competition, the best film award went to Chabname Zariab’s thriller When She Hears The Bells which follows a young widow who arrives in Kabul during the imminent takeover by the Taliban. The jury noted: “It is a tense, emotional story of resistance and courage that kept us on the edge of our seats.”
The top prize in the critics’ picks competition went to Maya Vitkova-Kosev’s Bulgarian drama One Month about a 45-year-old woman whose parents give her one month to move out.

In the Baltic film competition, Andrius Blaževičius’s How To Divorce During The War was awarded best feature film which comes with a €5,000 grant. The dark comedy is set in Lithuania and follows a woman who tells her husband she wants a divorce on the eve of Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
The audience award went to Louis Paxton’s Scottish comedy The Incomer, starring Domhnall Gleeson and Gayle Rankin.
